catalysts.headline: Generac reported Q3 2026 results before market open: record net sales of $1.29B (+16% YoY), GAAP net income $109M ($1.83/diluted share), adjusted net income $151M ($2.54/diluted share, beating the $2.44 consensus estimate), gross margin 39.9%, free cash flow $131.7M. Data-center product backlog grown to approximately $4.5 billion following the Amazon agreement and other wins (the Amazon deal itself still projects ~$2.4B of initial deliveries across 2027-2028). Maintained full-year 2026 net sales growth guidance in the mid-to-high-teens percent range; narrowed full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to approximately 20.5%-21.0%.

Generac disclosed a long-term supply agreement to provide backup generators for Amazon data centers, with aggregate potential gross payments of up to $8 billion over the life of the arrangement and roughly $2.4 billion of initial deliveries expected across 2027-2028. As part of the deal, Generac issued a warrant to an Amazon subsidiary for up to 1,693,745 shares at a $200.9266 strike price (one source instead describes the initial vesting tranche as 300,000 shares, with the remainder vesting as payments/deliveries occur — see conflicts).
catalysts.impact: Shares were up about 34.5% in premarket trading on the announcement; Cantor Fitzgerald kept its rating and called it the firm's most important data-center-related news item

catalysts.headline: Amazon obtained the right to buy up to $340M of Generac stock as part of a $2.4B backup-generator supply deal for AI data centers
catalysts.impact: stock recorded a record single-session gain the following day

catalysts.headline: Generac reported Q2 2026 results before the open: EPS of $2.91 on revenue of $1.17 billion (+10.6% YoY), with Commercial & Industrial external net sales up ~29% YoY to $556 million; revenue came in slightly below some analyst expectations. Management cited a data-center backlog of $1.6 billion as of July 2026 and said tariff refunds helped margins and cash flow; the Sussex, WI plant was said to be on track to begin production ahead of schedule.
